column1: The British sculptor Henry Moore was a leading figure in the 20th-century art world
column2: 英国雕塑家亨利·摩尔是20世纪艺术界的领军人物。

column1: Henry Moore was born in Castleford, a small town near Leeds in the north of England.
column2: 亨利·摩尔出生在英格兰北部利兹附近的小镇卡斯尔福德。

column1: He was the seventh child of Raymond Moore and his wife Mary Baker.
column2: 他是雷蒙德·摩尔和妻子玛丽·贝克的第七个孩子。

column1: He studied at Castleford Grammar School from 1909 to 1915, where his early interest in art was encouraged by his teacher Alice Gostick.
column2: 1909年至1915年，他在卡斯尔福德文法学校读书。老师艾丽斯·戈斯蒂克鼓励了他早年对艺术的兴趣。
column5: early interest in art|年少时对艺术的兴趣

column1: After leaving school, Moore hoped to become a sculptor, but instead he complied with his father’s wish that he train as a schoolteacher.
column2: 离校后，摩尔本想成为雕塑家，却顺从父亲的心愿，接受了师范训练。
column7: train as a schoolteacher|接受中小学教师培训

column1: He had to abandon his training in 1917 when he was sent to France to fight in the First World War.
column2: 1917年，他被派往法国参加第一次世界大战，只得中断训练。
column6: the First World War|第一次世界大战

column1: After the war, Moore enrolled at the Leeds School of Art, where he studied for two years.
column2: 战后，摩尔进入利兹艺术学院，在那里学习了两年。

column1: In his first year, he spent most of his time drawing.
column2: 第一年，他把大部分时间都用来画画。
column3: In his first year|在他就读的第一年
column4: spent most of his time|把大部分时间花在……上

column1: Although he wanted to study sculpture, no teacher was appointed until his second year.
column2: 尽管他想学雕塑，但校方直到第二年才任命雕塑教师。
column6: until his second year|直到他入学后的第二年

column1: At the end of that year, he passed the sculpture examination and was awarded a scholarship to the Royal College of Art in London.
column2: 那年年底，他通过了雕塑考试，并获得前往伦敦皇家艺术学院学习的奖学金。
column4: passed the sculpture examination|通过雕塑考试
column5: was awarded a scholarship|获颁奖学金
column6: Royal College of Art|皇家艺术学院

column1: In September 1921, he moved to London and began three years of advanced study in sculpture.
column2: 1921年9月，他迁往伦敦，开始了为期三年的雕塑深造。

column1: Alongside the instruction he received at the Royal College, Moore visited many of the London museums, particularly the British Museum, which had a wide-ranging collection of ancient sculpture.
column2: 在皇家艺术学院上课之余，摩尔还参观了伦敦许多博物馆，尤其是大英博物馆，那里收藏了种类繁多的古代雕塑。

column1: During these visits, he discovered the power and beauty of ancient Egyptian and African sculpture.
column2: 参观期间，他领略了古埃及和非洲雕塑的力量与美。
column3: During these visits|在这些参观中

column1: As he became increasingly interested in these ‘primitive’ forms of art, he turned away from European sculptural traditions.
column2: 随着对这些“原始”艺术形式的兴趣日益浓厚，他逐渐背离了欧洲雕塑传统。
column3: increasingly interested in|对……愈发感兴趣

column1: After graduating, Moore spent the first six months of 1925 travelling in France.
column2: 毕业后，摩尔用1925年的头六个月在法国旅行。
column4: the first six months|头六个月

column1: When he visited the Trocadero Museum in Paris, he was impressed by a cast of a Mayan* sculpture of the rain spirit.
column2: 参观巴黎特罗卡德罗博物馆时，一件玛雅雨神雕像的翻模复制品给他留下了深刻印象。

column1: It was a male reclining figure with its knees drawn up together, and its head at a right angle to its body.
column2: 那是一尊斜倚的男性人像，双膝并拢屈起，头转到与身体成直角。
column3: male reclining figure|斜倚的男性人像
column4: knees drawn up together|双膝并拢屈起
column5: at a right angle to|与……成直角

column1: Moore became fascinated with this stone sculpture, which he thought had a power and originality that no other stone sculpture possessed.
column2: 摩尔深深着迷于这件石雕。他觉得，其他任何石雕都没有它这样的力量与独创性。

column1: He himself started carving a variety of subjects in stone, including depictions of reclining women, mother-and-child groups, and masks.
column2: 他自己也开始用石头雕刻各种题材，包括斜倚的女性形象、母子群像和面具。
column4: a variety of subjects|各种题材

column1: Moore’s exceptional talent soon gained recognition, and in 1926 he started work as a sculpture instructor at the Royal College.
column2: 摩尔过人的才华很快得到认可。1926年，他开始在皇家艺术学院担任雕塑教师。

column1: In 1933, he became a member of a group of young artists called Unit One.
column2: 1933年，他加入了一个名为“一号团体”的青年艺术家团体。
column3: became a member of|成为……的一员
column4: a group of young artists|一群青年艺术家

column1: The aim of the group was to convince the English public of the merits of the emerging international movement in modern art and architecture.
column2: 这个团体旨在让英国公众认识到，当时正在兴起的国际现代艺术与建筑运动有其可取之处。

column1: Around this time, Moore moved away from the human figure to experiment with abstract shapes.
column2: 大约在这个时候，摩尔开始摆脱人体形象的束缚，尝试抽象造型。

column1: In 1931, he held an exhibition at the Leicester Galleries in London.
column2: 1931年，他在伦敦的莱斯特画廊举办展览。

column1: His work was enthusiastically welcomed by fellow sculptors, but the reviews in the press were extremely negative and turned Moore into a notorious figure.
column2: 雕塑界同行热烈欢迎他的作品，但报刊上的评论极为负面，摩尔也因此声名狼藉。
column5: reviews in the press|报刊评论

column1: There were calls for his resignation from the Royal College, and the following year, when his contract expired, he left to start a sculpture department at the Chelsea School of Art in London.
column2: 有人呼吁他从皇家艺术学院辞职。次年合同期满，他便离开皇家艺术学院，到伦敦切尔西艺术学院创办雕塑系。
column7: start a sculpture department|创办雕塑系

column1: Throughout the 1930s, Moore did not show any inclination to please the British public.
column2: 整个20世纪30年代，摩尔都没有表现出丝毫要迎合英国公众的意愿。
column6: please the British public|迎合英国公众

column1: He became interested in the paintings of the Spanish artist Pablo Picasso, whose work inspired him to distort the human body in a radical way.
column2: 他对西班牙画家巴勃罗·毕加索的画作产生了兴趣。在这些作品的启发下，他开始对人体形象作大胆的扭曲变形。
column6: distort the human body|扭曲人体形态
column7: in a radical way|以大胆而彻底的方式

column1: At times, he seemed to abandon the human figure altogether.
column2: 有时候，他似乎完全舍弃了人体形象。

column1: The pages of his sketchbooks from this period show his ideas for abstract sculptures that bore little resemblance to the human form.
column2: 这一时期的素描本记录了他的抽象雕塑构想，那些造型与人体形态已几乎没有相似之处。
column6: bore little resemblance to|与……几乎不相似

column1: In 1940, during the Second World War, Moore stopped teaching at the Chelsea School and moved to a farmhouse about 20 miles north of London.
column2: 1940年，正值第二次世界大战，摩尔停止在切尔西艺术学院任教，搬到伦敦以北约20英里的一处农舍。
column3: during the Second World War|在第二次世界大战期间

column1: A shortage of materials forced him to focus on drawing.
column2: 材料短缺迫使他把精力转向绘画。
column3: A shortage of materials|材料短缺

column1: He did numerous small sketches of Londoners, later turning these ideas into large coloured drawings in his studio.
column2: 他为伦敦人画了许多幅小素描，后来在工作室里把这些构思发展成大幅彩色画。
column6: turning these ideas into|把这些构思发展为

column1: In 1942, he returned to Castleford to make a series of sketches of the miners who worked there.
column2: 1942年，他回到卡斯尔福德，为当地矿工画了一系列素描。
column4: a series of sketches|一系列素描

column1: In 1944, Harlow, a town near London, offered Moore a commission for a sculpture depicting a family.
column2: 1944年，伦敦附近的哈洛镇委托摩尔创作一件表现一家人的雕塑。
column3: a town near London|伦敦附近的一个镇
column4: offered Moore a commission|委托摩尔创作
column6: depicting a family|表现一家人的形象

column1: The resulting work signifies a dramatic change in Moore’s style, away from the experimentation of the 1930s towards a more natural and humanistic subject matter.
column2: 这件作品标志着摩尔风格的一大转变：他离开了20世纪30年代的实验性探索，转向更自然、更富人文色彩的题材。

column1: He did dozens of studies in clay for the sculpture, and these were cast in bronze and issued in editions of seven to nine copies each.
column2: 他为这件雕塑做了几十件泥塑习作，随后用它们翻铸青铜像，每件习作各发行七至九件铸本。
column7: editions of seven to nine copies each|每种版数为七至九件

column1: In this way, Moore’s work became available to collectors all over the world.
column2: 这样一来，世界各地的收藏家都有机会收藏摩尔的作品。
column4: became available to|变得可供……取得
column6: all over the world|世界各地

column1: The boost to his income enabled him to take on ambitious projects and start working on the scale he felt his sculpture demanded.
column2: 收入增加后，他得以承接雄心勃勃的项目，也能按他心目中作品所需的体量来创作。
column3: boost to his income|收入的增长

column1: Critics who had begun to think that Moore had become less revolutionary were proven wrong by the appearance, in 1950, of the first of Moore’s series of standing figures in bronze, with their harsh and angular pierced forms and distinct impression of menace.
column2: 有些评论家一度认为摩尔的作品已不如从前具有革新精神。1950年，他的青铜立像系列推出首作，证明他们看错了。这些立像造型粗粝、棱角分明，雕有镂空，明显透出威胁感。
column5: were proven wrong|被证明判断有误
column6: standing figures in bronze|青铜立像
column7: harsh and angular|粗粝而棱角分明的

column1: Moore also varied his subject matter in the 1950s with such works as Warrior with Shield and Falling Warrior.
column2: 20世纪50年代，摩尔也以《持盾的战士》《倒下的战士》等作品拓宽了创作题材。

column1: These were rare examples of Moore’s use of the male figure and owe something to his visit to Greece in 1951, when he had the opportunity to study ancient works of art.
column2: 这些作品是摩尔少有的男性形象作品，其创作一定程度上得益于他1951年的希腊之行。当时他有机会在当地研究古代艺术品。
column5: owe something to|一定程度上得益于
column8: ancient works of art|古代艺术品

column1: In his final years, Moore created the Henry Moore Foundation to promote art appreciation and to display his work.
column2: 晚年，摩尔创立了亨利·摩尔基金会，以推广艺术欣赏并展出自己的作品。
column3: In his final years|在他的晚年

column1: Moore was the first modern English sculptor to achieve international critical acclaim and he is still regarded as one of the most important sculptors of the 20th century.
column2: 摩尔是第一位在国际艺评界赢得赞誉的英国现代雕塑家，至今仍被视为20世纪最重要的雕塑家之一。
column3: modern English sculptor|英国现代雕塑家
column5: international critical acclaim|国际艺评界的赞誉
column6: is still regarded as|仍被视为
column7: one of the most important|最重要的……之一
